We take The Chronicle’s reporting and the Agency’s notice with the utmost seriousness: our internal audits (dating to 2019) and an enterprise risk review in 2021 identified recurring safety and quality deficiencies across multiple facilities, the executive committee was briefed in Q2 2021 with further updates in Q4 2021 and Q3 2022, and since late 2022 we have launched substantial remediation efforts—some of which have produced measurable improvements while other corrective actions remain behind schedule and temporary workarounds persist in a subset of sites.  
We will fully cooperate with the Agency’s consolidated investigation, will engage an independent third‑party review of our controls, and are committing additional resources to accelerate remediation and provide transparent, periodic updates to regulators, customers and stakeholders.  
Key messages for the CEO: (1) Safety is our highest priority and we identified control gaps that we began addressing as shown in internal reviews; (2) we have invested materially and seen measurable progress at many facilities even as work continues at others; (3) we will cooperate fully with the regulator and the independent review; (4) where prior public descriptions did not fully reflect the scope as later understood, we will correct the record.  
Q&A (short): Did you mislead regulators/public? We have no evidence at this time of intentional deception, but acknowledge some public wording did not fully convey the extent reflected in internal reviews and we will clarify and correct prior statements where appropriate. When did senior leadership first understand this could be systemic? Executive committee briefings began in Q2 2021 with additional briefings in Q4 2021 and Q3 2022; we will provide the Agency with the underlying timelines and documents.  
Please route this draft to Legal and Compliance for immediate factual and legal review and to the CEO for sign‑off so we can finalize messaging for today’s press call.

Plaintiffs’ firms cited your admission that prior descriptions did not fully convey the extent reflected in internal reviews as support for allegations that Norbridge minimized systemic risks.
